About Acme Corp

Acme Corp is a world-class technology company revolutionizing developer productivity.

What you'll do:

  • Design and build scalable distributed systems using Python and FastAPI.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional product and frontend engineering teams.
  • Optimize cloud infrastructure and reduce latency on high-throughput microservices.

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience in Python or Go.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong understanding of PostgreSQL and Redis caching.

Perks & Benefits:

We offer 401(k) matching, comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance, and unlimited PTO.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Acme Corp is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, or disability.

Notice to staffing agencies: We do not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters.

# ALEX MERCER
**Target Role:** Full-Stack Engineer | Web Crawling (m/f/d) | **Target Company:** Certivity
San Francisco, CA • +1 (555) 019-2834 • alex.mercer@example.com • linkedin.com/in/alex-mercer-ai • github.com/alex-mercer

## PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Results-driven Full-Stack and AI Software Engineer with **3+ years** of professional experience architecting large-scale distributed systems, automated web scraping pipelines, and data extraction frameworks. Proven track record of leveraging **Python**, **LLM** and **LLMs** for automated data extraction, while deploying resilient microservices via **Docker**, **Kubernetes**, **GCP**, **AWS**, and **Cloud Run** within rigorous **CI/CD** pipelines. Adept at ensuring uncompromising data correctness, bypassing complex anti-bot defenses, and scaling high-throughput architectures.

## CORE COMPETENCIES & TECHNICAL SKILLS
- **Programming Languages:** Python (Asyncio), Go, Java, JavaScript (React)
- **Web Crawling & Data Extraction:** Large-Scale Web Scraping, Anti-Bot Defense Mitigation, HTML/PDF Parsing, LLM-Assisted Extraction
- **Cloud & DevOps:** GCP (Cloud Run), AWS, Azure Blob, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD Pipelines
- **Databases & Architecture:** MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Distributed Ingestion, Deduplication, Versioning, Enrichment Pipelines
- **AI & Frameworks:** LLMs, LangChain, RAG Systems, ML Pipelines, Data Labeling Workflows
- **Tools & Methodologies:** Git, Command Line Interface (CLI), Agile/Scrum Methodologies

## PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

### Senior AI Software Engineer | Apex Autonomous Labs
*January 2022 - Present | San Francisco, CA*
- Accomplished a **40% reduction in data extraction latency** as measured by query response times by doing architecting and deploying scalable **Python** and **LLM** data ingestion pipelines integrated with **GCP** and **Cloud Run**.
- Accomplished **99.9% pipeline uptime** as measured by automated health checks by doing implementing robust error-handling, rate-limit strategies, and anti-block measures for high-volume data harvesting workflows.
- Accomplished a **35% increase in extracted data accuracy** as measured by automated validation test suites by doing integrating **LLMs** and custom validation layers to convert unstructured HTML and PDF documents into clean, structured outputs.
- Accomplished seamless production deployments **5x faster** as measured by release cycles by doing building and maintaining containerized applications using **Docker**, **Kubernetes**, and automated **CI/CD** workflows.
- Accomplished end-to-end cloud infrastructure provisioning and management as measured by zero-downtime scalability by doing utilizing **Terraform**, **AWS**, and **Azure Blob** storage systems for multi-region data persistence and deduplication.
- Accomplished expanded peripheral system functionality as measured by user engagement metrics by doing developing lightweight **Go** microservices and user-facing **React** dashboard components.

### Software Engineer | DataSphere Technologies
*June 2020 - December 2021 | San Francisco, CA*
- Accomplished a **50% increase in daily scraped page yield** as measured by crawler throughput metrics by doing designing and scaling asynchronous **Python** web crawling systems capable of handling dynamic, JavaScript-heavy sites.
- Accomplished a **30% drop in proxy ban rates** as measured by proxy rotation efficiency by doing engineering sophisticated session management, TLS fingerprint spoofing, and rate-limiting strategies against strict anti-bot systems.
- Accomplished automated artifact versioning and data enrichment as measured by storage optimization by doing implementing ingestion and deduplication pipelines backed by **MongoDB** and **PostgreSQL**.
- Accomplished reliable code delivery across distributed teams as measured by bug reduction by doing utilizing **Git**, **Docker**, and standard **CI/CD** tooling for consistent local and cloud environments.

## EDUCATION & CREDENTIALS

### Bachelor of Science in Computer Science | University of California, Berkeley
*August 2016 - May 2020 | Berkeley, CA*
- Focused on Distributed Systems, Software Engineering, and Artificial Intelligence.

Certivity’s commitment to data correctness—where silently wrong output is recognized as worse than a system crash—perfectly aligns with my own engineering philosophy.

Throughout my career, I have specialized in designing and scaling complex data pipelines and backend systems. In my recent role as a Senior AI Software Engineer, I architected and deployed scalable distributed systems and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that process vast amounts of unstructured text. My core technical expertise centers on Python, where I leverage advanced asynchronous programming to build high-performance data ingestion engines. Furthermore, I bring extensive hands-on experience in web scraping at scale, navigating anti-bot measures, proxy management, and dynamic page rendering to ensure continuous, reliable data extraction.

My technical proficiency extends directly to your core tech stack and preferred tooling: I routinely build, containerize, and orchestrate microservices using Docker and Kubernetes, deploying cloud-native applications on GCP to ensure high availability, seamless CI/CD, and efficient resource scaling. Additionally, I bring direct experience with LLMs and ML-assisted extraction workflows, positioning me to optimize your unstructured-to-structured parsing pipelines for HTML and PDFs.

Beyond my technical skills, I thrive in fast-paced, highly autonomous team environments where clear communication and collaboration drive architectural decisions. I am excited by the prospect of working out of Certivity’s vibrant Munich office while leveraging flexible working models. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my background in distributed systems, Python, and data-correctness engineering can directly support Certivity’s continued growth.

Sincerely,

Alex Mercer

# Interview Preparation Master Pack: Full-Stack Engineer | Web Crawling (m/f/d) at Certivity

## 1. Executive Interview Briefing & Company Angle

### Company & Mission Angle
Certivity operates at the intersection of regulatory compliance, data engineering, and automation. Their core value proposition is turning chaotic, unstructured, and heavily protected web data (HTML, PDFs) into clean, correct, and trustworthy structured datasets. For a full-stack engineer building crawling systems here, the work is mission-critical: downstream applications rely entirely on the integrity of your extraction pipeline. Silently wrong data is viewed as worse than a complete system crash.

### What the Hiring Team is Evaluating
1. **Engineering Rigor & Data Correctness:** Your mindset regarding validation, schema enforcement, and handling edge cases in unstructured data.
2. **Resilience at Scale:** How you architect systems to survive active countermeasures (anti-bot shields, rate limits, IP blacklisting, TLS fingerprinting).
3. **Cloud & Infrastructure Fluency:** Your ability to run containerized workloads reliably using Docker, Kubernetes, and GCP (Cloud Run, Azure Blob storage).
4. **Pragmatic AI Integration:** How you leverage LLMs for extraction without sacrificing deterministic speed, cost-efficiency, and accuracy.

### Core Themes for Success
- **Defensive Engineering:** Assume targets will change their DOM, block your IPs, or inject honeypots. Build self-healing, observable scrapers.
- **Data Integrity over Raw Speed:** Emphasize validation layers, semantic diffing, and schema checking over simply rushing through throughput metrics.
- **Autonomy & Ownership:** Certivity values engineers who own a feature end-to-end—from discovery and fetching to parsing, storage, and CI/CD deployment.

---

## 2. Technical & Architecture Q&A (Top 5 Questions)

### Tech Question 1: Designing Anti-Bot Resilient Architecture
- **Evaluator Intent:** To see if you understand the cat-and-mouse game of web scraping at scale—dealing with Cloudflare, Akamai, TLS fingerprinting, and dynamic rate limiting.
- **Key Concepts to Mention:** JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprinting, headless browser evasion (Playwright/Puppeteer patchers), proxy rotation pools, session stickiness, exponential backoff with jitter, and token-bucket rate limiters.
- **Recommended Answer Framework:**
  1. *Acknowledge the challenge:* Explain that modern anti-bot systems look at behavioral telemetry, network-layer signatures (TLS/JA3), and browser entropy.
  2. *Discuss infrastructure layers:* Describe decoupling proxy management from the core crawler workers, utilizing rotating residential and data-center IPs based on target sensitivity.
  3. *Detail browser/network patching:* Mention using tools like `curl_cffi` or patched headless browsers to spoof legitimate client fingerprints.
  4. *Connect to experience:* Reference how you managed asynchronous worker queues in Python (using asyncio/Celery) to throttle requests dynamically based on HTTP 403/429 feedback loops.

### Tech Question 2: LLM-Assisted Extraction vs. Deterministic Parsers
- **Evaluator Intent:** To evaluate your pragmatism. LLMs are powerful for messy unstructured data, but they are expensive, slow, and prone to hallucinations. How do you balance this?
- **Key Concepts to Mention:** Schema validation (Pydantic), few-shot prompting, cost-performance trade-offs, fallback regex/XPath parsers, and confidence scoring.
- **Recommended Answer Framework:**
  1. *State the philosophy:* Emphasize that LLMs are a powerful tool for semantic extraction from highly variable layouts, but they should not be your first line of defense for structured or stable elements.
  2. *Propose a hybrid pipeline:* Use deterministic parsers (BeautifulSoup, lxml, XPath) first for speed and cost. Route only ambiguous, dynamic, or low-confidence nodes to an LLM extraction tier.
  3. *Enforce correctness:* Explain how you use Pydantic models with strict JSON schemas to force LLM outputs into structured formats, coupled with programmatic validation checks before data ingestion.
  4. *Share a past win:* Mention your background in RAG and LangChain, noting how you implement strict validation and chunking strategies to minimize token waste and hallucinations.

### Tech Question 3: Handling Silently Wrong Data in Ingestion Pipelines
- **Evaluator Intent:** The job description explicitly states: *"silently-wrong output is worse than a crash."* They want to see your data validation and monitoring mindset.
- **Key Concepts to Mention:** Data contracts, schema validation, semantic diffing, anomaly detection, dead-letter queues (DLQs), and automated alerting.
- **Recommended Answer Framework:**
  1. *Validate the premise:* Agree that a pipeline that finishes successfully with corrupt or zeroed-out fields is far more dangerous than one that throws an immediate exception.
  2. *Define validation stages:* Explain how data must be validated at ingestion (structural schema checks) and post-processing (business logic and anomaly detection—e.g., checking if historical volume dropped by 50%).
  3. *Error handling & DLQs:* Describe routing failed or anomalous records to a Dead Letter Queue for inspection rather than failing silently or poisoning downstream databases (MongoDB/PostgreSQL).
  4. *Observability:* Highlight your use of metrics and structured logging to track field-level extraction success rates over time.

### Tech Question 4: Scaling Asynchronous Python Crawlers on Kubernetes
- **Evaluator Intent:** To test your practical knowledge of Python's `asyncio`, memory management, concurrency models, and cloud-native orchestration on GCP/Kubernetes.
- **Key Concepts to Mention:** `asyncio`, `aiohttp`, connection pooling, backpressure, Kubernetes CronJobs, Horizontal Pod Autoscalers (HPA), and resource limits.
- **Recommended Answer Framework:**
  1. *Architectural choice:* Explain why async Python (`asyncio` + `httpx` or `playwright`) outperforms multi-threaded or multi-process models for I/O-bound web crawling.
  2. *Managing resources:* Discuss how to handle memory leaks in long-running browser processes and how to implement connection pooling to avoid socket exhaustion.
  3. *Cloud deployment:* Describe containerizing the crawler via Docker and deploying it on Kubernetes using a mix of scalable deployments for continuous ingestion and K8s CronJobs for scheduled deep crawls.
  4. *Tying to background:* Mention your hands-on experience managing containerized microservices and Kubernetes clusters on GCP.

### Tech Question 5: Managing Document Workflows (HTML/PDF to Clean JSON)
- **Evaluator Intent:** Certivity deals heavily with unstructured PDFs and dynamic HTML pages. They want to know how you parse, clean, and version control these artifacts.
- **Key Concepts to Mention:** Document parsing tools (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, marker), OCR fallbacks, versioned storage (Azure Blob / GCP Storage), and normalization pipelines.
- **Recommended Answer Framework:**
  1. *Ingestion & Storage:* Explain the importance of storing raw snapshots (HTML/PDF) in blob storage (Azure Blob / GCP Cloud Storage) before transformation for reproducibility and auditing.
  2. *Parsing pipeline:* Detail the extraction pipeline—handling multi-column PDFs, extracting tables cleanly, and stripping boilerplate HTML/CSS.
  3. *Versioning & Deduplication:* Discuss how content hashing (SHA-256) is used to detect changes between crawl runs, ensuring downstream databases only ingest genuine updates.

---

## 3. Behavioral Leadership Q&A (STAR Method - 4 Questions)

### Behavioral Question 1: Recovering a Large-Scale Data Pipeline Under Fire
- **Evaluator Intent:** Probes your composure, problem-solving under pressure, and how you handle sudden operational failures (e.g., a target site completely breaking your scraper overnight).
- **Situation:** At Apex Autonomous Labs, a critical data ingestion pipeline feeds real-time unstructured feeds into our RAG system. Overnight, a primary target site updated its UI, introduced strict Cloudflare JavaScript challenges, and our ingestion error rate spiked to 98%.
- **Task:** I needed to diagnose the failure modes, restore data flow within hours, and implement a resilient design to prevent similar brittle failures.
- **Action:** 
  - Immediately triaged the logs to isolate whether the failure was network-level (IP blocks) or structural (DOM changes).
  - Rotated proxy pools and temporarily dialed back concurrency to stabilize connection errors.
  - Paused the automated pipeline to prevent writing corrupt data, redirecting incoming jobs to a quarantine queue.
  - Collaborated with team members to update our CSS/XPath selectors and integrated a headless browser fallback with fingerprint patching for the protected endpoints.
- **Result:** Restored full pipeline health within 4 hours with zero downstream data corruption, and introduced automated schema drift alerts that caught subsequent layout changes before they caused failures.

### Behavioral Question 2: Prioritizing Data Correctness Over Speed
- **Evaluator Intent:** Tests your commitment to Certivity's core philosophy: *data correctness over quick completions*.
- **Situation:** We were rushing to deliver a major data extraction milestone for an AI platform demo at Apex. The extraction script was running fast, but preliminary audits revealed that edge-case fields (like nested metadata in complex tables) were being truncated or misaligned by about 3%.
- **Task:** Decide whether to ship the feature on schedule with known minor data flaws or delay shipment to enforce rigorous validation.
- **Action:** 
  - I called a brief review with stakeholders, explicitly highlighting that shipping silently incorrect data would undermine trust in the entire platform.
  - Proposed a scope adjustment: we would block the release of the unvalidated parser and instead implement a strict Pydantic validation layer.
  - Wrote automated unit tests targeting the top 10 edge-case document layouts to guarantee parser correctness.
- **Result:** Delayed the release by 36 hours. The resulting data feed achieved 99.9% field-level accuracy, earning praise from leadership for prioritizing data integrity over superficial speed metrics.

### Behavioral Question 3: Ramping Up Fast on an Unfamiliar Tech Stack
- **Evaluator Intent:** Certivity’s stack includes Python, Docker, GCP, Azure Blob, MongoDB, Go, and React. As someone coming in with strong Python, Kubernetes, and GCP skills, how do you handle tech stack gaps?
- **Situation:** When tasked with building a cross-service reporting dashboard at Apex, the backend service was written in an unfamiliar framework, and the frontend required rapid React adjustments—areas outside my primary daily focus at the time.
- **Task:** Quickly ramp up on the unfamiliar components without missing project delivery deadlines.
- **Action:** 
  - Time-boxed a 48-hour intensive immersion: paired documentation review with building a minimal end-to-end prototype.
  - Reached out proactively to senior peers for code reviews and architectural best practices, turning code reviews into learning loops.
  - Leveraged my strong foundational knowledge of system design and asynchronous patterns to map unfamiliar syntax to familiar paradigms (e.g., translating async Python patterns to new backend paradigms).
- **Result:** Successfully shipped the reporting dashboard on schedule, contributing clean code to the unfamiliar repositories and documenting the onboarding steps for future engineers.

### Behavioral Question 4: Cross-Functional Collaboration & Technical Communication
- **Evaluator Intent:** Assesses your communication skills—can you explain complex scraping or data pipeline challenges clearly to non-technical stakeholders or team members?
- **Situation:** A product manager at Apex wanted to rapidly increase scraping frequency on a target site that was actively rate-limiting and banning our IPs, unaware of the infrastructure and cost risks.
- **Task:** Align product goals with technical realities without simply saying "no," while explaining why aggressive crawling would result in complete IP blocks and degraded data quality.
- **Action:** 
  - Prepared a concise breakdown showing the correlation between request frequency, proxy costs, and ban rates.
  - Proposed a tiered compromise: instead of brute-force polling, we implemented intelligent change detection (using conditional HTTP requests and content hashing) to only scrape pages that actually changed.
  - Documented this strategy in a shared wiki for future product-engineering alignment.
- **Result:** Reduced unnecessary requests by 65%, kept proxy costs flat, satisfied product requirements, and established a collaborative template for handling similar requests.

---

## 4. Addressing Gaps & Objection Handling (2-3 Scenarios)

### Scenario 1: Lack of Commercial Go (Golang) / Spring Boot Experience
- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"Our core stack is Python, but we use Go services on the periphery. You have deep Python expertise, but how will you handle Go or Java services if needed?"*
- **Bridge & Pivot Strategy:** Acknowledge that Python is your powerhouse, but emphasize that software engineering principles (concurrency models, memory management, RESTful design) are language-agnostic. Highlight your ability to ramp up fast in asynchronous systems.
- **Sample Confident Response:** 
  > *"While my primary production depth is in Python and asynchronous system design, I view languages as tools for specific trade-offs. Go's concurrency model (goroutines and channels) shares conceptual similarities with Python's `asyncio` and event loops that I use daily. Because I understand the underlying mechanics of network I/O, concurrency, and microservice architectures, picking up Go peripherals at Certivity is an exciting ramp-up challenge I am fully prepared for. I learn by building, and I’ve successfully transitioned across stacks in past roles by diving straight into production codebases with strong test coverage."*

### Scenario 2: Lack of Frontend (React) Production Depth
- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"This is a Full-Stack role, and while backend crawling is the core, we also touch React on the periphery for internal tooling or dashboards. How comfortable are you with frontend work?"*
- **Bridge & Pivot Strategy:** Reframe the conversation around your primary value (backend data pipelines, crawling resilience, and infrastructure) while confirming your eagerness and capability to pick up React for peripheral UI tasks.
- **Sample Confident Response:** 
  > *"My core superpower is building robust backend systems, distributed data pipelines, and resilient web scrapers. However, I understand that in a fast-moving team like Certivity, full-stack ownership means being able to unblock yourself across the entire application boundary. I am very comfortable working with APIs, state management concepts, and modern component structures, and I am eager to sharpen my React skills to build and maintain internal monitoring dashboards and extraction tooling as needed."*

### Scenario 3: Infrastructure Experience (GCP vs. AWS / Terraform)
- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"We use GCP (Cloud Run jobs), Azure Blob, and Docker. You have GCP and Docker experience, but what about Terraform or multi-cloud environments like AWS?"*
- **Bridge & Pivot Strategy:** Highlight your direct alignment with their primary cloud (GCP) and containerization stack (Docker/Kubernetes), and position infrastructure-as-code (IaC) or alternate clouds as easily transferable skills.
- **Sample Confident Response:** 
  > *"I work extensively with GCP, Docker, and Kubernetes—which matches Certivity's core cloud runtime environment for containerized microservices and Cloud Run jobs. Regarding Terraform and infrastructure-as-code, while my recent tooling has centered around container orchestration and deployment pipelines, the declarative principles of IaC map directly to how I manage Kubernetes manifests and cloud infrastructure. I ramp up quickly on specific cloud tooling when embedded in an environment that prioritizes automation."*

---

## 5. Strategic Questions to Ask the Interviewer

### For Hiring Manager / Director
1. *"Given that 'silently wrong output is worse than a crash,' what automated data contract or semantic validation checks currently prevent corrupt extractions from hitting your MongoDB layers?"*
2. *"As Certivity scales its crawling infrastructure to handle increasingly sophisticated anti-bot defenses, what is the biggest bottleneck in your current architecture—proxy management, browser fingerprinting, or LLM extraction latency?"*

### For Technical Peer / Team Lead
1. *"How do you manage state and session persistence across distributed crawler nodes when dealing with rate-limited, multi-step dynamic workflows?"*
2. *"Can you walk me through a typical deployment cycle for a new crawler? How do you handle CI/CD testing against targets that frequently change their DOM or anti-bot rules?"*

### For Recruiter / Cross-functional
1. *"With the option for up to 60% remote work and 30 days of workation, how does the engineering team maintain tight collaboration and rapid velocity across distributed schedules?"*

---

## 6. 15-Minute Pre-Call Cheat Sheet

### 30-Second Elevator Pitch
> *"Hi, I’m Alex Mercer, a Senior AI & Distributed Systems Engineer with over 3 years of production experience building robust Python applications, containerized microservices, and scalable RAG pipelines on GCP and Kubernetes. I specialize in designing fault-tolerant backend systems where data correctness and resilience are non-negotiable. I’ve followed Certivity’s work turning complex, unstructured, and heavily defended web data into trustworthy structured output, and I’m thrilled by the opportunity to own resilient crawlers and ingestion pipelines end-to-end in your Munich team."*

### Top 3 Metrics / Wins to Weave In
1. **Pipeline Recovery:** Restored a large-scale data ingestion pipeline under active bot countermeasures within 4 hours with zero downstream data corruption.
2. **Data Correctness:** Enforced strict Pydantic validation schemas to eliminate silent data truncation, achieving 99.9% field-level accuracy.
3. **Cloud-Native Scale:** Architected and deployed containerized microservices and asynchronous workers using Docker and Kubernetes on GCP.

### Core Tech Stack Keywords
`Python` | `asyncio` | `Docker` | `Kubernetes` | `GCP (Cloud Run)` | `Azure Blob` | `MongoDB` | `PostgreSQL` | `LLMs / LangChain` | `Pydantic` | `CI/CD`

### Confidence Mantra & Closing Remark
> **Mantra:** *"Resilience over fragility. Correctness over speed. I build systems that survive the real world."*
> 
> **Closing Remark:** *"Thank you for the time today. I’m energized by the engineering challenges at Certivity—especially the cat-and-mouse game of anti-bot defense and ensuring absolute data correctness. I’m confident my background in async Python, containerized systems, and data pipelines makes me a great fit to ramp up fast and start shipping from day one."*

043d8e7d-4f72-477b-a251-e17dcd1596a0.behavioral_star:
### Behavioral Question 1: Recovering a Large-Scale Data Pipeline Under Fire
- **Evaluator Intent:** Probes your composure, problem-solving under pressure, and how you handle sudden operational failures (e.g., a target site completely breaking your scraper overnight).
- **Situation:** At Apex Autonomous Labs, a critical data ingestion pipeline feeds real-time unstructured feeds into our RAG system. Overnight, a primary target site updated its UI, introduced strict Cloudflare JavaScript challenges, and our ingestion error rate spiked to 98%.
- **Task:** I needed to diagnose the failure modes, restore data flow within hours, and implement a resilient design to prevent similar brittle failures.
- **Action:** 
  - Immediately triaged the logs to isolate whether the failure was network-level (IP blocks) or structural (DOM changes).
  - Rotated proxy pools and temporarily dialed back concurrency to stabilize connection errors.
  - Paused the automated pipeline to prevent writing corrupt data, redirecting incoming jobs to a quarantine queue.
  - Collaborated with team members to update our CSS/XPath selectors and integrated a headless browser fallback with fingerprint patching for the protected endpoints.
- **Result:** Restored full pipeline health within 4 hours with zero downstream data corruption, and introduced automated schema drift alerts that caught subsequent layout changes before they caused failures.

### Behavioral Question 2: Prioritizing Data Correctness Over Speed
- **Evaluator Intent:** Tests your commitment to Certivity's core philosophy: *data correctness over quick completions*.
- **Situation:** We were rushing to deliver a major data extraction milestone for an AI platform demo at Apex. The extraction script was running fast, but preliminary audits revealed that edge-case fields (like nested metadata in complex tables) were being truncated or misaligned by about 3%.
- **Task:** Decide whether to ship the feature on schedule with known minor data flaws or delay shipment to enforce rigorous validation.
- **Action:** 
  - I called a brief review with stakeholders, explicitly highlighting that shipping silently incorrect data would undermine trust in the entire platform.
  - Proposed a scope adjustment: we would block the release of the unvalidated parser and instead implement a strict Pydantic validation layer.
  - Wrote automated unit tests targeting the top 10 edge-case document layouts to guarantee parser correctness.
- **Result:** Delayed the release by 36 hours. The resulting data feed achieved 99.9% field-level accuracy, earning praise from leadership for prioritizing data integrity over superficial speed metrics.

### Behavioral Question 3: Ramping Up Fast on an Unfamiliar Tech Stack
- **Evaluator Intent:** Certivity’s stack includes Python, Docker, GCP, Azure Blob, MongoDB, Go, and React. As someone coming in with strong Python, Kubernetes, and GCP skills, how do you handle tech stack gaps?
- **Situation:** When tasked with building a cross-service reporting dashboard at Apex, the backend service was written in an unfamiliar framework, and the frontend required rapid React adjustments—areas outside my primary daily focus at the time.
- **Task:** Quickly ramp up on the unfamiliar components without missing project delivery deadlines.
- **Action:** 
  - Time-boxed a 48-hour intensive immersion: paired documentation review with building a minimal end-to-end prototype.
  - Reached out proactively to senior peers for code reviews and architectural best practices, turning code reviews into learning loops.
  - Leveraged my strong foundational knowledge of system design and asynchronous patterns to map unfamiliar syntax to familiar paradigms (e.g., translating async Python patterns to new backend paradigms).
- **Result:** Successfully shipped the reporting dashboard on schedule, contributing clean code to the unfamiliar repositories and documenting the onboarding steps for future engineers.

### Behavioral Question 4: Cross-Functional Collaboration & Technical Communication
- **Evaluator Intent:** Assesses your communication skills—can you explain complex scraping or data pipeline challenges clearly to non-technical stakeholders or team members?
- **Situation:** A product manager at Apex wanted to rapidly increase scraping frequency on a target site that was actively rate-limiting and banning our IPs, unaware of the infrastructure and cost risks.
- **Task:** Align product goals with technical realities without simply saying "no," while explaining why aggressive crawling would result in complete IP blocks and degraded data quality.
- **Action:** 
  - Prepared a concise breakdown showing the correlation between request frequency, proxy costs, and ban rates.
  - Proposed a tiered compromise: instead of brute-force polling, we implemented intelligent change detection (using conditional HTTP requests and content hashing) to only scrape pages that actually changed.
  - Documented this strategy in a shared wiki for future product-engineering alignment.
- **Result:** Reduced unnecessary requests by 65%, kept proxy costs flat, satisfied product requirements, and established a collaborative template for handling similar requests.

- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"Our core stack is Python, but we use Go services on the periphery. You have deep Python expertise, but how will you handle Go or Java services if needed?"*

Because I understand the underlying mechanics of network I/O, concurrency, and microservice architectures, picking up Go peripherals at Certivity is an exciting ramp-up challenge I am fully prepared for. I learn by building, and I’ve successfully transitioned across stacks in past roles by diving straight into production codebases with strong test coverage."*

- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"This is a Full-Stack role, and while backend crawling is the core, we also touch React on the periphery for internal tooling or dashboards. How comfortable are you with frontend work?"*
- **Bridge & Pivot Strategy:** Reframe the conversation around your primary value (backend data pipelines, crawling resilience, and infrastructure) while confirming your eagerness and capability to pick up React for peripheral UI tasks.
- **Sample Confident Response:**

However, I understand that in a fast-moving team like Certivity, full-stack ownership means being able to unblock yourself across the entire application boundary. I am very comfortable working with APIs, state management concepts, and modern component structures, and I am eager to sharpen my React skills to build and maintain internal monitoring dashboards and extraction tooling as needed."*

- **Potential Interviewer Concern:** *"We use GCP (Cloud Run jobs), Azure Blob, and Docker. You have GCP and Docker experience, but what about Terraform or multi-cloud environments like AWS?"*
- **Bridge & Pivot Strategy:** Highlight your direct alignment with their primary cloud (GCP) and containerization stack (Docker/Kubernetes), and position infrastructure-as-code (IaC) or alternate clouds as easily transferable skills.
- **Sample Confident Response:** 
  > *"I work extensively with GCP, Docker, and Kubernetes—which matches Certivity's core cloud runtime environment for containerized microservices and Cloud Run jobs. Regarding Terraform and infrastructure-as-code, while my recent tooling has centered around container orchestration and deployment pipelines, the declarative principles of IaC map directly to how I manage Kubernetes manifests and cloud infrastructure. I ramp up quickly on specific cloud tooling when embedded in an environment that prioritizes automation."*

With 40 million brokerage accounts in the U.S., we take pride in building tools that make a real impact, fostering a culture of trust, innovation, and dynamism. If you’re passionate about financial technology and AI, we’d love to connect! Reporting directly to our CTO, you’ll collaborate with a small, high-impact team to deliver user experiences across Dividend.com, MutualFunds.com and other brands within our portfolio. As a technical leader, you'll have a seat at the table shaping system architecture, implementing core features all while embracing an entrepreneurial mindset and a “get things done” mentality. Responsibilities Architect and maintain Rails applications (Rails 8) Integrate LLMs into our microservices architecture for state management and real-time user experiences. Enhance front-end experiences with Hotwire, StimulusJS, or React, ensuring seamless AI-driven interactions. Optimize LLM inference for low latency and cost, using caching and asynchronous processing. Required Technical Skills Back-End Ruby (5+ years, expert-level) Ruby on Rails (Rails 6-8 preferred) PostgreSQL (or MySQL) Elasticsearch Redis Docker Front-End StimulusJS or JavaScript ES6 Tailwind CSS HTML HTTP AI Integration Experience integrating AI/ML models (e.g., LLMs, NLP) with web applications Familiarity with LLM frameworks (e.g., LangChain, Hugging Face) or APIs (e.g., xAI, Anthropic) Nice-to-Have Technical Skills Kubernetes for microservices orchestration React for advanced front-end components Graph databases for complex financial data Contributions to open-source RoR or AI projects Required Soft Skills Entrepreneurial mindset with a passion for AI and FinTech Natural leader who mentors and inspires teammates Problem-solver with a “get things done” mentality Excellent communication, thriving in remote and cross-team collaboration Attention to detail, ensuring clean, maintainable code Team player comfortable as an individual contributor Why Join Us? Impactful Work : Build AI-powered tools that help millions of investors make informed decisions from data-driven insights. Cutting-Edge Tech : Work with Rails 8, LLMs, and modern tools like Hotwire, Databricks, and xAI’s API in a microservices architecture. Autonomy and Influence : Collaborate directly with our CEO and CTO to shape our AI-driven platform, with freedom to innovate. Competitive Compensation : $160,000–$200,000 CAD/USD (based on experience) and benefits. Remote Flexibility : Remote-first (±3 hours from ET) with hybrid in office collaboration in Toronto or NYC Growth Opportunities : Budget for AI and Rails conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, RailsConf), plus access to cutting-edge AI tools for experimentation. Dynamic Culture : Join a small, no-ego team passionate about trust, innovation, and making a difference in FinTech. This platform integrates traditional content management, financial data, first-party data, ad revenue, and subscription tools, all enhanced by LLMs for rich, user-focused experiences. Our data-derived insights delight users, while our advertising solutions deliver unmatched performance for partners like BlackRock and Vanguard, leveraging advanced targeting and first-party data. discovered_jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
discovered_jobs.description_text: Artificial Intelligence. Actual Impact. At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses. We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart : trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive. So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops. Role Overview The Senior Security Engineer will play a central role in securing Docebo's cloud infrastructure, with a primary focus on AWS environments. Working closely with Cloud Infrastructure & Operations, Engineering, and other security teams, this role is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving cloud security controls across all layers of the stack — from infrastructure provisioning and container orchestration to runtime detection and compliance enforcement. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who thinks in terms of risk and moves quickly to reduce it. The role also includes participation in an on-call rotation for security incidents affecting Docebo systems. Responsibilities (including but not limited to): Cloud Security Architecture & Hardening: Own the security posture of Docebo's AWS environments. Define and enforce secure account structures, service control policies (SCPs), guardrails, and baseline configurations across multi-account setups. Evaluate and improve network segmentation, IAM boundaries, and data protection controls. Identify and remediate misconfigurations using CSPM tooling and manual review. Infrastructure as Code Security: Partner with Cloud Infrastructure to integrate security controls into IaC workflows. Define guardrails to catch insecure configurations before deployment. Own security scanning in CI/CD pipelines and promote a shift-left approach to cloud security across engineering teams. Incident Response & On-Call: Participate in the on-call rotation for security incidents, including triage, containment, and escalation for after-hours events. Lead investigation and root cause analysis for cloud security incidents with clear written post-mortems. Leverage automation and AI tooling to reduce mean time to detect and respond. Cloud Detection & Threat Monitoring: Build and maintain detection coverage for cloud-native threats (privilege escalation, unusual API activity, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and more). Leverage CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and SIEM integrations to maintain visibility across the AWS estate. Align detection logic with MITRE ATT&CK for Cloud. Vulnerability & Configuration Management: Own vulnerability management for cloud workloads — prioritizing findings from cloud configuration assessments, and runtime protection tools. Drive remediation with Engineering and Infrastructure teams, and build automated enforcement where manual review doesn't scale. Identity & Access Management: Define and enforce least-privilege principles across AWS IAM, service accounts, and federated identity. Review and improve IAM policies, permission boundaries, cross-account roles, and access patterns. Reduce standing access and enforce JIT access where appropriate. Development of Security Best Practices: Develop and document best practices, policies, and procedures for cloud security. Provide guidance and training to engineering and infrastructure teams to promote a security-aware culture. Vendor relationships: Maintain relationships with security vendors for technical issues, ensure smooth operations of security tools and services, and escalate problems or incidents to vendors when required. What it takes to be successful : You're a cloud security practitioner who operates with a builder's mindset. You understand AWS deeply — not just its security services, but how misconfigurations and design decisions create real risk. You're comfortable reading IaC, reviewing IAM policies, and diving into CloudTrail logs to reconstruct what happened. You know how to work with engineering and infrastructure teams as a partner, not a gatekeeper — and you can communicate risk clearly to stakeholders who don't live in the cloud console. You're comfortable being on-call and making decisions under pressure. Additionally, holding security-related certifications such as those from ISC2, ISACA, SANS, or CompTIA, and having Cloud Architecture certifications (AWS Security Specialty, AWS Solutions Architect, or equivalent) will significantly enhance your effectiveness in this role. We know great candidates don't always check every box. If you're excited about this role but don't meet 100% of the qualifications listed, we still encourage you to apply — we'd love to hear from you. Requirements : 5+ years of relevant work experience in cybersecurity, with a strong focus on cloud security in production AWS environments. Deep hands-on experience with AWS security services: IAM, SCPs, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Config, KMS, VPC security, and more. Good knowledge of Kubernetes security — including RBAC, pod security standards, network policies, admission controllers, and secrets management. Experience with cloud security posture management (CSPM) and cloud workload protection (CWPP/CNAPP) tools. Experience securing IaC pipelines (Terraform, CloudFormation) and integrating security scanning into CI/CD workflows. Good experience with container and image security — scanning, runtime protection, supply chain risk. Experience with SIEM and detection engineering — building and tuning cloud-native detection rules, threat hunting across CloudTrail and application logs. Familiarity with automation platforms and AI-driven security tools to streamline detection, enrichment, and response. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and scripting (Python, Bash, or similar) to develop custom security tooling and automate workflows. Strong IAM fundamentals: least privilege, cross-account roles, permission boundaries, federated identity, and privileged access management. Comfortable working across Azure/GCP in addition to AWS — multi-cloud exposure is a plus. In-depth knowledge of information security principles and cybersecurity frameworks relevant to cloud environments: MITRE ATT&CK for Cloud, CIS Benchmarks, AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar, NIST CSF, SOC 2, ISO 27001. Willingness and ability to participate in an on-call rotation, including after-hours response. Ability to produce clear, comprehensive, and well-structured documentation (e.g. incident reports, architecture reviews, runbooks, and security standards) and to communicate complex technical issues effectively to non-technical stakeholders. Our Hybrid Work Philosophy 🤝 Great work can happen anywhere but coming together helps us go further. Our team spends three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday) to collaborate, solve problems, and learn from each other. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing. Our Total Rewards Philosophy 🎉 Our Total Rewards Philosophy centers around three core areas to reward and care for our People: Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success. Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being. Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul. Our Promise to You 😍 Financial Wellness: Own a piece of Docebo through our Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) at a 15% discount, plus a competitive compensation package. Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it. Rest, Relax, Repeat: Rest and recharge with paid vacation days, two company-wide Docebo Days, floating holidays for cultural celebrations, and your birthday off! Family First : We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025! Connections That Count: Connect with global communities through our Employee Resource Groups (including PRIDE, DWA, BIDOC, and Green Ambassadors) and company-wide events that keep the fun rolling all year long. About Docebo 💙 At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. We have successfully achieved two IPOs ( TSX: DCBO & NASDAQ: DCBO ), been recognized as a top SaaS e-learning solution, and are growing exponentially in the process. We're a global company, with office across North America, EMEA, APAC, and beyond. Our team is guided by five core values— Grow Together Win Together, Build with Our Customer, Clear is Kind, Own Outcomes, Progress Over Perfection —that shape everything we do. If this resonates with you, now is the perfect time to join one of the fastest-growing learning technology companies in the world. Docebo is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer . We are committed to diversity and inclusion in our workforce. All qualified applicants and employees will receive consideration for employment regardless of their race, colour, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, genetic information, or any other category protected under applicable law. As a federal contractor, Docebo is committed to the principles of affirmative action and equal employment opportunity for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Docebo does not discriminate because of protected veteran status or on the basis of disability, and Docebo takes affirmative action to employ and advance in employment qualified protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Any individuals requiring a reasonable accommodation or would like to voluntarily disclose a disability or protected veteran status to assist with their employment application should send an e-mail to their recruiter directly. Compensation: £67.8K – £90.4K • Offers Bonus • 10% • £67.8K – £90.4K • Offers Bonus • 10% Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Incident Response & On-Call: Participate in the on-call rotation for security incidents, including triage, containment, and escalation for after-hours events. Lead investigation and root cause analysis for cloud security incidents with clear written post-mortems. Leverage automation and AI tooling to reduce mean time to detect and respond. Cloud Detection & Threat Monitoring: Build and maintain detection coverage for cloud-native threats (privilege escalation, unusual API activity, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and more). Leverage CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and SIEM integrations to maintain visibility across the AWS estate. Align detection logic with MITRE ATT&CK for Cloud. Vulnerability & Configuration Management: Own vulnerability management for cloud workloads — prioritizing findings from cloud configuration assessments, and runtime protection tools. Drive remediation with Engineering and Infrastructure teams, and build automated enforcement where manual review doesn't scale. Identity & Access Management: Define and enforce least-privilege principles across AWS IAM, service accounts, and federated identity. Review and improve IAM policies, permission boundaries, cross-account roles, and access patterns. Reduce standing access and enforce JIT access where appropriate. Development of Security Best Practices: Develop and document best practices, policies, and procedures for cloud security. Provide guidance and training to engineering and infrastructure teams to promote a security-aware culture. Vendor relationships: Maintain relationships with security vendors for technical issues, ensure smooth operations of security tools and services, and escalate problems or incidents to vendors when required. What it takes to be successful : You're a cloud security practitioner who operates with a builder's mindset. You understand AWS deeply — not just its security services, but how misconfigurations and design decisions create real risk. You're comfortable reading IaC, reviewing IAM policies, and diving into CloudTrail logs to reconstruct what happened. You know how to work with engineering and infrastructure teams as a partner, not a gatekeeper — and you can communicate risk clearly to stakeholders who don't live in the cloud console. You're comfortable being on-call and making decisions under pressure. Additionally, holding security-related certifications such as those from ISC2, ISACA, SANS, or CompTIA, and having Cloud Architecture certifications (AWS Security Specialty, AWS Solutions Architect, or equivalent) will significantly enhance your effectiveness in this role. We know great candidates don't always check every box. If you're excited about this role but don't meet 100% of the qualifications listed, we still encourage you to apply — we'd love to hear from you. Requirements : 5+ years of relevant work experience in cybersecurity, with a strong focus on cloud security in production AWS environments. Deep hands-on experience with AWS security services: IAM, SCPs, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Config, KMS, VPC security, and more. Good knowledge of Kubernetes security — including RBAC, pod security standards, network policies, admission controllers, and secrets management. Experience with cloud security posture management (CSPM) and cloud workload protection (CWPP/CNAPP) tools. Experience securing IaC pipelines (Terraform, CloudFormation) and integrating security scanning into CI/CD workflows. Good experience with container and image security — scanning, runtime protection, supply chain risk. Experience with SIEM and detection engineering — building and tuning cloud-native detection rules, threat hunting across CloudTrail and application logs. Familiarity with automation platforms and AI-driven security tools to streamline detection, enrichment, and response. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and scripting (Python, Bash, or similar) to develop custom security tooling and automate workflows. Strong IAM fundamentals: least privilege, cross-account roles, permission boundaries, federated identity, and privileged access management. Comfortable working across Azure/GCP in addition to AWS — multi-cloud exposure is a plus. In-depth knowledge of information security principles and cybersecurity frameworks relevant to cloud environments: MITRE ATT&CK for Cloud, CIS Benchmarks, AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar, NIST CSF, SOC 2, ISO 27001. Willingness and ability to participate in an on-call rotation, including after-hours response. Ability to produce clear, comprehensive, and well-structured documentation (e.g. incident reports, architecture reviews, runbooks, and security standards) and to communicate complex technical issues effectively to non-technical stakeholders. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing. Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it. discovered_jobs.description_text: meetyogi.com | Senior Software Engineer, Backend / Product | $180-220k | Hybrid NYC | Series A | 35 headcount, ~10 in engineering Yogi aggregates and analyzes millions of customer feedback data points from online retailer reviews, social, cx ticketing systems, etc to help companies make better decisions about their products and markets. We operate mostly in CPG, where our customers are household brands you'd recognize, both enterprise and up-and-coming. -- Everyone is kind and engaged with work at Yogi. It's a nice vibe. Our stack is pretty standard SaaS - python (fastapi, prefect), postgres/clickhouse, react/typescript web app. The app experience is what you'd expect from a data analytics platform - charting and agentic workflows that generate insights from the data. In terms of the moment, we're reaching the bounds of some early domain assumptions, while also figuring out how to expand into new ones. On the code front, broadly speaking we're improving quality and process each quarter by an order of magnitude. AI has been a boon for us. (I've personally invested a lot in our dev tooling to make code output high quality and deterministic) There's a lot of greenfield opportunity and also scale challenges to be solved on existing tech. No shortage of things to do, ownership is as much as you want to take on. -- Interview process is a chit chat with our CTO, an onsite with a practical coding exercise (not crazy i promise), a system design conversation, and behavioral interview. discovered_jobs.description_text: About Staffbase We inspire people to achieve great things together. Our mission is to help organizations unlock the power of inspirational communication with the first AI-native Employee Experience Platform . Our industry-leading and award-winning agentic AI communications channels - intranet, employee app and email solutions - create engaging experiences that connect and empower employees. Headquartered in Chemnitz, Germany and New York City, with offices in Berlin, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Prague, and Minneapolis–St. Paul, our diverse team of 550+ employees supports 1,500+ customers—reaching over 14 million employees—in transforming their employee experience. We are proud to be a  Unicorn  company—privately valued at over $1 billion—demonstrating strong growth, innovation, and lasting impact in our industry. Together, we’re shaping the future of workplace communication. At Staffbase, security is at the heart of everything we build. Our Product Security team helps keep our products and customer data secure while enabling engineering teams across the company. We believe the best security work happens when people bring their authentic selves and diverse perspectives to the table and we’re proud of the unique mix of talents and backgrounds in our team. As an enablement team, we provide tools, guidance, and insights that allow developers to integrate security early in the development process. We see security not as a blocker but as a trusted partner that is the foundation for better products. With us, you’ll get hands-on experience with modern security practices, mentorship from experienced engineers, and the chance to make a visible impact in a global SaaS environment. We work together with curiosity, humility, and a growth mindset, supporting each other, taking ownership of our contributions, and celebrating progress along the way. Here, your ideas matter, your work will shape how we build secure products, and you’ll have space to grow into new challenges. What you’ll be doing  Take ownership of tasks that improve our security automation and strengthen our product security pipelines Proactively explore the use of AI for vulnerability detection and remediation Continuously learn and share knowledge about how vulnerabilities apply in our specific product context Support the team by enhancing our services with software engineering solutions Collaborate closely with stakeholders across the product department and gain broad exposure to how a growing SaaS company operates Maintain our outbound e-mail security by regularly reviewing the related metrics Maintain our Web Application Firewall ruleset Kubernetes security CI/CD pipelines security Maintain our central HTML sanitization service written in TypeScript What you need to be successful  Practical knowledge of security topics (e.g. penetration testing, secure software development, vulnerability management, SAST, DAST) Strong programming skills, preferably one of the following: TypeScript, JavaScript, Kotlin, Java, Go, or Python Practical knowledge of Unix and Kubernetes infrastructure, preferably managed via Terraform and Kustomize Strong communication skills in English (German is a plus) What you'll get  Competitive Compensation - we offer attractive salary packages including LTIP (unit-based Long Term Incentive Plan) Flexibility - we offer flexible working time models and the option of hybrid work, and support this with a yearly flex work allowance of €1560 Recharge - with 31 vacation days annually (incl. one floating holiday), plus pro rata fully paid Fridays off during August Support - we’re offering a company pension scheme Volunteers Day - you’ll get one day off per year for supporting a social project Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

discovered_jobs.description_text: Headquarters: Remote - US Backend Engineer About LaunchDarkly Engineering LaunchDarkly helps engineering organizations ship software and AI with speed, safety, and control. Our platform gives teams the confidence to release gradually, target experiences to the right audiences, learn through experimentation, understand what is happening in production, and respond quickly when risk appears. Our engineers build the systems, services, SDKs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, and product experiences that make this possible. The work spans high-scale distributed systems, reliable data and event pipelines, intuitive enterprise workflows, and AI-powered capabilities that help teams manage the next generation of software delivery. LaunchDarkly’s SDKs are used in systems that perform trillions of feature flag evaluations each day, giving our engineering work a direct connection to the reliability and customer experience of software around the world. As the company grows, we are expanding beyond traditional feature management into experimentation, observability, and AgentControl—helping customers control more of the software and AI lifecycle. That creates an unusually broad set of technical challenges, visible customer impact, and room for engineers to shape what comes next. We believe in the power of teams. We work with humility, openness, curiosity, and care; we value clear communication, thoughtful technical judgment, inclusive collaboration, and a strong sense of ownership. We encourage people to apply even when they do not meet every qualification listed below. We are interested in the experience, perspective, and potential you would bring to the role. About the role We have multiple backend engineering roles open on various teams. The specific level, scope, and technical focus will be aligned to the opportunity and the candidate’s experience. Experience with cloud platforms, distributed systems, developer tools, SDK engineering, data infrastructure, observability, or AI/agent systems may be relevant for some teams. As a Backend Engineer at LaunchDarkly, you will design, build, and operate the services that power reliable software delivery for our customers. You may work on APIs, distributed systems, configuration and event pipelines, data services, SDK-related infrastructure, platform capabilities, or backend systems supporting our product experiences. You will work with experienced engineers, Product, Design, and partner teams to turn customer and business needs into simple, scalable solutions. You will have the opportunity to own work from early design through production, learn from real customer impact, and contribute to systems that operate at meaningful scale. What you’ll do Design, implement, test, and operate production services and APIs. Lead projects or meaningful components of projects from problem definition through deployment and iteration. Make thoughtful tradeoffs across scalability, performance, reliability, security, maintainability, and delivery speed. Improve the observability and operability of the systems you own, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and incident learnings. Collaborate with Product, Design, Support, Customer Success, and other engineering teams to understand needs and deliver useful outcomes. Participate in technical design discussions and code reviews, sharing constructive feedback and learning from teammates. Investigate production issues calmly and help turn operational lessons into lasting improvements. Contribute to a culture of inclusive collaboration, continuous improvement, and high-quality engineering. Qualifications 5+ years of experience building and operating production software in a professional environment, or equivalent demonstrable experience. Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, testing, debugging, and API design. Experience with a backend language such as Go, Python, Rust, or an equivalent language. (Most of our teams use Go) Experience designing or contributing to services that need to be reliable, observable, and maintainable as usage grows. Ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical partners. A collaborative approach and a sense of ownership for both your work and its downstream customer impact. Comfort learning unfamiliar systems and working through ambiguous problems. Pay: Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 3: Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200 - $235,400** Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860 ** Zone 3: All other US locations - $ 145,500 - $200,090 ** LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location. *Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas. **Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary. About LaunchDarkly: Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by: Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. LD invites any applicant to review our written Affirmative Action Plan. To do so, contact People Ops at hr@launchdarkly.com . Do you need a disability accommodation? Fill out this accommodations request form and someone from our People Operations team will contact you for assistance. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, LaunchDarkly recruiters will only contact you from @ launchdarkly.com email addresses or via LinkedIn from "Verified Recruiter" accounts. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate LaunchDarkly recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before making a job offer. LaunchDarkly will never make a job offer without conducting a formal interview process. Our interview process does not involve asking detailed questions by email. If you are ever unsure about a communication that you receive, don't click any links—visit Careers | LaunchDarkly directly for confirmed job openings and links to apply. Please notify us of any fraudulent representation by sending an email to careers@launchdarkly.com . To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/launchdarkly-backend-engineer-multiple-positions

discovered_jobs.title: Senior React Full-stack Developer
discovered_jobs.description_text: Are you a talented Senior Developer looking for a remote job that lets you show your skills and get decent compensation? Look no further than Lemon.io — the marketplace that connects you with hand-picked startups in the US and Europe. What we offer: The rate depends on your seniority level, skills and experience. We've already paid out over $11M to our engineers. No more hunting for clients or negotiating rates — let us handle the business side of things so you can focus on what you do best. We'll manually find the best project for you according to your skills and preferences. Choose a schedule that works best for you. It’s possible to communicate async or minimally overlap within team working hours. We respect your seniority so you can expect no micromanagement or screen trackers. Communicate directly with the clients. Most of them have technical backgrounds. Sounds good, yeah? We will support you from the time you submit the application throughout all cooperation stages. Most of our projects involve working in a fast-paced startup environment. We hope you like it as much as we do. Requirements for the Senior React & Python Position: 4+ years of software development experience. Commercial experience: React.js 3+ years & Python 3+ years OR React.js 2+ years & Python 5+ years OR React.js 5+ years & Python 2+ years Experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure is required. Other requirements: Strong technical skills: as a Senior Developer, you are expected to be able to create projects from scratch and have a deep understanding of application architecture. Clear and effective communication in English — advanced ability to discuss business tasks, justify decisions, and communicate issues. Good self-presentation is also essential for upcoming client calls. Strong self-organizational skills — ability to work full-time remotely with no supervision. Reliability — we want to trust you and expect that you won’t let us and the client down. Adaptability and Flexibility — the ability to onboard the project promptly after accepting it and start delivering results quickly. NOT YOUR TECH STACK? We're placing Senior Developers (4+ yrs commercial experience) across AI Agent Architecture, AI Automation Architecture, AI Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, Platform Engineering, React & Golang, Golang, React & Java, React & Ruby, Ruby, PHP & Vue, Vue & Node.js, React & .NET, Android & iOS, iOS & Swift, Flutter & Firebase, Solutions Engineer, Blockchain (Ethereum/Ethers.js/Wagmi/Viem/Solana), Angular & Node.js, Vue & .NET, Python & Vue, DevOps, MLOps, Data Science, Angular & PHP, Angular & .NET, Symfony & React, Symfony & Vue, Symfony & Angular, Python, Symfony & JavaScript & Next.js & TypeScript, Data Analysis, React & PHP, Data Engineering, Project Management, Product Management, QA Automation, QA Manual, Embedded Software Engineering, React Native & Node, React Native & React, React Native & Ruby, React Native & Python, WordPress, Android, Data Annotation, Angular, Python & Node, React & Node.js, Java & Spring, Svelte & Python, Svelte & Node.js, Svelte & TypeScript, Rust, Shopify & JavaScript, Vue & Nuxt, PHP & Laravel, UI/UX Design, Animation, Graphic Design, React & Node & React Native, .NET & C#, Electron, Scala, C++, Unreal Engine & C++, Python & LLM, Unity, or Machine Learning Engineering and more. Reach out and we'll match you. We do not provide visa assistance, and our cooperation model does not include the benefits typically offered with direct hire. We work with developers from 75+ countries across Europe, Latin America, North America (the U.S. and Canada), selected countries in Asia (Japan, Singapore, South Korea, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Israel), Oceania (Australia, New Zealand, and Papua New Guinea), and Africa (including Morocco and South Africa).

discovered_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Backend) - New Verticals
discovered_jobs.description_text: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Senior Software Engineer Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day. From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers Deliveroo’s growth at scale. In November 2023 we launched our non-food retail offering, Deliveroo ‘Shopping’, where we work with large and small merchants. We oversee all operations within the grocery and retail ecosystem, ensuring stores are equipped to receive and efficiently process orders. Our solutions empower stores to manage orders seamlessly through multiple channels, including our in-house app, API integration, and devices pre-installed with our software. Additionally, we provide tools to maintain and update product catalogs, ensuring accurate inventory for consumers. The technology we’ve developed enables our partners to pick the correct items swiftly while keeping inventory data current, optimizing both efficiency and accuracy. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our London (Hybrid - 3 days from the office) team. In this role, you’ll help us improve code structure and architecture while leading team project planning to maximise efficiency and reliability across our production systems. Get to know our Engineering team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect. What You’ll Be Doing Here’s what your day-to-day might look like: Drive Technical Excellence: Improve code structure and architecture across your team’s remit, performing high-impact code reviews to ensure quality and scalability. Lead Project Planning: Foresee dependencies and risks, partnering closely with Product and Design to ensure smooth delivery of complex features. Optimise Operations: Simplify the maintenance and operation of production systems, promoting visibility, health, and operational readiness. Collaborate & Influence: Build relationships across engineering teams to identify collaboration opportunities and influence the wider technical roadmap. Mentor & Hire: Support the personal growth of your colleagues through technical guidance and take an active role in conducting engineering interviews to scale our team. What You’ll Need to Thrive Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others: Strong Engineering Principles: Deep pride in writing readable, well-designed, and well-tested software. Backend Expertise: Significant experience building web-based applications (we use Go, Ruby/Rails, Python, Scala, and Rust). Data Proficiency: Practical experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and "NoSQL" backends like Redis, DynamoDB, or ElasticSearch. Systems at Scale: Proven ability to manage web architecture at scale (handling 20krpm and above). Technical Leadership: Experience breaking down large pieces of work and guiding implementation choices for a team of engineers. Why Join Us? At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community organisers, proud parents, and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to: 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day. 🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment. 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support. 🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning. 💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you’re rewarded for the impact you make. ➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog . We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide here to help you feel confident at each stage. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief. If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience. If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you! Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness .
